questions.stem: India's primary spaceport, from which the vast majority of ISRO launches take place, is located at Sriharikota. In which state does this spaceport fall?

options.option_text: Tamil Nadu, on the Coromandel Coast near Chennai city
Andhra Pradesh, on Sriharikota island in the Bay of Bengal
Odisha, near Wheeler Island launch facility on the eastern coast
Karnataka, near Bengaluru where ISRO's main headquarters is situated

questions.explanation: Sriharikota is a barrier island in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh; the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) there hosts ISRO's two launch pads. Tamil Nadu (A) is a common confusion because Sriharikota is geographically close to the TN border. Wheeler Island in Odisha (C) is a missile testing range, not ISRO's satellite launch site. ISRO's HQ is in Bengaluru, Karnataka (D), but that city has no launch pad.

questions.stem: Chandrayaan-1 (2008), India's first lunar mission, produced a landmark scientific result that reshaped understanding of the Moon. What was that discovery?

options.option_text: First detection of helium-3 reserves trapped in the lunar regolith layer
Confirmation of permanently shadowed lava tubes beneath the lunar near-side
Discovery of water molecules and hydroxyl radicals on the lunar surface
First mapping of subsurface ice deposits at the lunar south polar crater rims

questions.explanation: NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3) instrument aboard Chandrayaan-1 detected spectral signatures of water (H2O) and hydroxyl (OH) in 2009, the first unambiguous confirmation of lunar surface water. Helium-3 (A) has been theorised but not definitively 'detected' by Chandrayaan-1. Lava tubes (B) and south-polar ice mapping (D) were not Chandrayaan-1 discoveries; south-polar ice confirmation came via later missions and the Moon Impact Probe crash data.

questions.stem: ISRO's LVM3 rocket (formerly GSLV Mk III) achieved its first dedicated commercial satellite launch mission in October 2022, marking a major step for India's commercial space sector. Whose satellites did it carry?

options.option_text: Planet Labs USA, deploying Dove earth-observation cubesats into SSO
OneWeb Ltd (UK), for its low-Earth-orbit broadband internet constellation
Amazon Project Kuiper, for broadband internet connectivity in South Asia
Telesat Canada, deploying LEO Phase-1 broadband satellites into orbit

questions.explanation: LVM3-M1 mission (October 2022) carried 36 OneWeb Gen-1 satellites into LEO, making it LVM3's first fully commercial flight — and the first time a non-ISRO payload rode the rocket. Planet Labs (A) has used PSLV, not LVM3. Amazon Kuiper (C) and Telesat (D) are real LEO constellation competitors but have not contracted LVM3; they are plausible distractors because both are broadband satellite firms with LEO plans.

questions.stem: The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), established in 2020, was created to fulfil which primary mandate?

options.option_text: Build and operate government communication satellites on behalf of ISRO
Regulate and promote private-sector participation in Indian space activities
Conduct commercial satellite launches as a successor to Antrix Corporation
Oversee India's military reconnaissance satellite programmes exclusively

questions.explanation: IN-SPACe is an autonomous single-window body under the Department of Space that authorises, promotes, and hand-holds non-governmental entities (startups, private firms) wishing to use ISRO facilities or conduct independent space activities. Antrix Corporation (A/C) remains ISRO's commercial arm for satellite-based services; IN-SPACe is distinct and focused on enabling the private sector rather than replacing Antrix. Defence satellite oversight (D) falls under DRDO/Defence Ministry, not IN-SPACe.

questions.stem: ISRO's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) is designed to serve the commercial small-satellite market. Which operational characteristic most sharply distinguishes it from PSLV in terms of launch readiness?

options.option_text: SSLV uses a cryogenic upper stage, whereas PSLV relies on a solid third stage
SSLV requires only ~72 hours of integration time versus PSLV's several weeks
SSLV can launch payloads to geostationary transfer orbit, unlike PSLV
SSLV employs a Vikas liquid-fuelled first stage, unlike PSLV's solid core

questions.explanation: The key selling point of SSLV for the commercial rideshare market is its minimal launch-preparation time — roughly 72 hours — versus PSLV which needs 45–70 days of integration and checkout. All three stages of SSLV are solid-propellant (no cryogenic stage — A is wrong). SSLV is designed only for LEO/SSO, not GTO (C is wrong). SSLV's first stage is also solid, not the Vikas liquid engine that powers PSLV's second stage (D is wrong).

questions.stem: Among PSLV's four variants — CA, G, QL, and XL — the PSLV-XL configuration carries six enlarged solid strap-on boosters of approximately 12 tonnes propellant each. In which ISRO mission was the PSLV-XL configuration first used operationally?

options.option_text: PSLV-C11, which carried Chandrayaan-1 to the Moon in October 2008
PSLV-C25, which launched Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) in November 2013
PSLV-C37, which simultaneously launched a record 104 satellites in 2017
PSLV-C5, the first operational PSLV mission in September 2002

questions.explanation: PSLV-C11 (Chandrayaan-1, October 22, 2008) was the maiden flight of the PSLV-XL variant, equipped with six 12-tonne strap-on boosters instead of the standard 9-tonne ones, needed to inject Chandrayaan-1 into a high Earth Transfer Orbit en route to the Moon. Mangalyaan (PSLV-C25) also used PSLV-XL, but it was not the first (B is a tempting distractor because Mangalyaan is well-remembered). The 104-satellite mission (PSLV-C37) used PSLV-XL too, but again not the first use. PSLV-C5 used the earlier Generic (G) variant.

questions.stem: ISRO's SPADEX (Space Docking Experiment), launched in December 2024, successfully demonstrated autonomous in-orbit docking between two small spacecraft in early 2025. Mastery of this technology is most specifically mission-critical for which upcoming ISRO project that requires rendezvous and docking in lunar orbit?

options.option_text: Gaganyaan extended mission, requiring crew transfer to the Bharatiya Antariksh Station
Chandrayaan-4 lunar sample return, which needs docking of ascent and transfer modules in lunar orbit
Shukrayaan-1 Venus orbiter, requiring deep-space trajectory correction manoeuvres
NISAR dual-frequency SAR satellite, a joint NASA-ISRO Earth observation mission

questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-4 is a lunar sample return mission whose architecture involves a lander-ascent module collecting soil samples and then docking with a transfer module in lunar orbit before returning to Earth — the exact capability SPADEX was designed to validate. BAS (A) also needs docking, but the Bharatiya Antariksh Station rendezvous is in LEO, not lunar orbit; SPADEX is expressly cited as the technology demonstrator for Chandrayaan-4's orbital docking. Shukrayaan-1 (C) and NISAR (D) require no in-orbit docking at all.
